deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 52–54). The data is (X, Σ, R): X is a compact oriented surface with boundary ∂X. Σ is a closed 1-submanifold of cutting circles ('cercles de découpage'). R is a finite set of marked points ('repères') on Σ. The combinatorial shadow of this data is a 'graphe pondéré à repères':
- vertices = components of X cut along Σ, weighted by genus;
- ordinary edges A_0 = π0(Σ);
- free edges A_ℓ = π0(∂X);
- marked points lying over edges.
The marked points are encoded by a set R⃗ carrying an action of the infinite dihedral group D_∞ = Z/2 * Z/2, generated by two involutions σ0 and σ1. This is a 1-dimensional analogue of the cartographic-group description of maps: each circle is subdivided by its marked points, and the D_∞-orbits are the circles. Grothendieck is defining elementary 'gommage' (erasing) operations, which become functors between groupoids of such structures (on p. 52 these are S_*TD^±_top, with a commutative diagram to the 'Gr. fond.' functor).

Item 1 (end; begun on p. 52): erasing a set R' of marked points. On the weighted graphs this corresponds to deleting a σ0,σ1-stable (D_∞-stable) subset R⃗' ⊂ R⃗.

Item 2, 'gommage de cercles de découpage':
- Choose a closed 1-submanifold Σ' ⊂ Σ \ ∂X, i.e. a union of components of Σ. Equivalently, choose a subset A'_0 ⊂ π0(Σ) = A_0 of ordinary edges.
- Replace Σ by Σ \ Σ'.
- On graphs, this contracts each edge of A'_0 to a point. The result is a new weighted graph together with a 'générisation' morphism from the old graph to the new one, the opposite of specialization.
- Grothendieck notes that one must make explicit how the weights follow, but does not write it out. The intended rule is the standard one: a contracted connected subgraph becomes one vertex of genus Σ g(v) + b1(subgraph).
- Marked points lying on Σ' are erased at the same time: on the graph one deletes all marks above edges in A'_0.

Purpose: build the combinatorial skeleton ('Lego') of the Teichmüller tower. Pants-type decompositions give the strata. Erasing circles is the combinatorial counterpart of moving from a deeper boundary stratum of the Deligne–Mumford compactification to a more generic one. Erasing marks and capping holes (item 3, next page) give the other 'forgetful' functors. Item 4 (next page) treats mixed simultaneous erasings.
errors: No error, but a gap: the rule for how the genus weights transform under edge contraction is announced ('Il convient ici d'expliciter comment la pondération suit...') and left unwritten.

Slight tension: erasing individual marked points R' (item 1) is said to correspond to a D_∞-stable subset of R⃗. A D_∞-stable subset is a union of whole orbits (whole circles' flag sets) under the reading above. So either R⃗ is not the flag set of the subdivided circles, or the stability condition needs refinement. This cannot be settled from this page.

ideas.what: Contracting a set of edges of a genus-weighted dual graph when cutting circles are erased, giving a generization morphism (old graph → new graph) opposite to specialization
ideas.modern_name: Edge contraction in the category of stable graphs; boundary stratification of the Deligne–Mumford compactification M̄_{g,n} (specialization/generization of strata)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford 1969, Knudsen 1983; graph-category formalism by Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower, pants decompositions and its 'Lego'. This explicit edge-contraction functor is not spelled out there as far as I know.

ideas.what: Marked points ('repères') on the cutting circles, encoded combinatorially by a set with an action of D_∞ = <σ0,σ1>, erased together with their circle
ideas.modern_name: Rigidified pants decompositions (marked points on cutting curves fixing the twist parameter); 1-dimensional cartographic-group encoding
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hatcher–Thurston 1980, Moore–Seiberg 1989, Bakalov–Kirillov 2000 (Lego-Teichmüller game); Grothendieck's cartographic groups via dessins (Esquisse)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups, Lego-Teichmüller), only in general terms

ideas.what: Erasing operations ('gommages') organised as functors between groupoids of decorated surfaces, compatible with the fundamental-group functor
ideas.modern_name: Forgetful / clutching-type functors in the Teichmüller tower; modular-operad structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) in outline; Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps for the Grothendieck–Teichmüller tower
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme, §2–3 (Teichmüller tower as a 'tour' of groupoids with operations)

missed.claim: The page is a 1983 manuscript record of a fully combinatorial set-up for the Teichmüller tower. It includes erasing operations on genus-weighted graphs with marks, and a D_∞-action encoding of the marks on cutting circles. This predates published Lego-Teichmüller treatments (Bakalov–Kirillov, Lochak–Schneps) and anticipates the stable-graph-category formalism (Getzler–Kapranov). Mathematically the content is standard today.
missed.quote: Au niveau des graphes pondérés, cela se traduit par une opération de contraction en un point des arêtes correspondantes, d'où formation d'un nouveau graphe, et d'un morphisme de générisation
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's precise combinatorial model behind the Esquisse's 'Lego'. The D_∞ (two-involution) encoding of marked circles could be compared with cartographic-group descriptions used in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (edge contraction of weighted dual graphs as generization, erasing marks with circles) is standard Deligne–Mumford stratification combinatorics. The only modest interest is the early date and the D_∞ encoding of marked circles.
transcription_corrections: 'graphes pondérés à rubans' should most likely read 'graphes pondérés à repères'. The same reading applies at the end: 'sur le graphe pondéré à repères, on fait sauter l'ensemble des repères qui sont au-dessus des arêtes ∈ A'_0'. R appears to be a set of marked points (repères), not ribbons.
Marginal insertion '{+sommets+} {+(rubans)+}' and 'sommets rubanés' are probably 'sommets (repérés)' / 'les sommets repérés se trouvant sur Σ''.
'd'une morphisme de générisation' is better read 'd'un morphisme de générisation'.
The insertion above 'fermée' read as '(sous-fibré)' is uncertain; it may be something like '(non vide)' or another qualifier.
